strengths: First TTA framework specifically designed for VLODs, addressing a genuine gap in the literature

Well-motivated technical approach with clear intuition: IWE exploits spatial coherence to reduce confirmation bias, IPS addresses prompt averaging limitations (Figures 1-2 effectively illustrate both)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 96 test scenarios, 2 VLOD architectures (CNN/Transformer-based), diverse distribution shifts (texture/style/driving/illumination/corruptions), consistent improvements across all settings
Thorough ablation studies: hyperparameter sensitivity, adapter placement effects, batch size, augmentation, prompt strategies, backbone robustness across both YOLO-World and Grounding DINO
Practical approach: single adaptation step, modest overhead (20 FPS), parameter-efficient (1.61M vs 76.81M for full fine-tuning), preserves zero-shot capability
Technically sound implementation: IoU graph construction well-defined, zero-initialization ensures no degradation, weights treated as constants during backprop
Strong empirical gains on corrupted data (PASCAL-C: +3.9 AP50) and style shifts (+3-5 mAP), with particularly notable improvements on digital corruptions (+8.2 JPEG, +7.0 Glass Blur)
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: IWE is intuitive but not conceptually novel (IoU weighting is straightforward), IPS simply selects top-ρ prompts by mean similarity without principled justification (why average vs. max? why hard selection vs. soft weighting?), adapters and residual prompt vectors borrowed from prior work

Modest improvements in key scenarios: driving scenes show only +1.0 mAP on Cityscapes/BDD100K, low-light only +1.2-1.9 mAP (ExDark), and acknowledged failure on small objects with low overlap limits real-world applicability

Core assumption lacks validation: claim that IoU-overlapping boxes indicate correct class isn't rigorously justified—overlaps could involve multiple object instances or class confusion. No empirical validation of this key assumption's reliability

Hyperparameter sensitivity and generalization concerns: multiple hyperparameters (θ, γ, λ, ρ, M) with dataset-dependent optimal values (θ optimal at 0.7 for Watercolor vs. 0.5 for Comic); no principled selection method provided, raising overfitting and generalization concerns

Insufficient analysis of mechanisms: limited quantitative analysis of why IWE works beyond intuition; Figure 11 provides one qualitative example but broader mechanism analysis missing; unclear under what conditions IWE outperforms standard entropy

Experimental inconsistencies: text embeddings computed offline for YW but during adaptation for GD (inconsistent treatment); main experiments use small models (YW-small, GD-Tiny) with limited analysis of scaling to larger models; unclear how much gain comes from adapters alone vs. IWE+IPS design

Prompt generation analysis: dataset-specific prompts yield +1.0 to +1.7 AP50 over GPT prompts, raising questions about how much improvement comes from TTA mechanism vs. prompt quality; limited exploration of alternative prompt fusion strategies

Missing ablations: no complete removal of IWE or IPS to isolate individual contributions; no alternative weighting schemes explored; architectural insights limited (why different adapter placements help different models)
Code availability: paper states 'Code:' but no actual link provided, hampering reproducibility verification

Theoretical gaps: no convergence analysis, no formal justification relating IoU clustering to improved generalization, relationship between entropy minimization on clustered proposals and domain adaptation performance unclear

strengths: Addresses a timely and important gap: first TTA framework specifically designed for VLODs, a practically relevant problem given the emergence of open-vocabulary detectors
Clear and effective motivation with good visual examples (Figures 1-2) illustrating failure modes of naive approaches
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across diverse distribution shifts, two different VLOD architectures, and 96 test scenarios with extensive ablations
Consistent improvements across all tested scenarios and multiple metrics
Practical design using lightweight adapters and single-step adaptation suitable for deployment; good reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: IoU-weighted entropy is a straightforward extension of standard entropy; image-conditioned prompt selection is a basic ranking strategy; residual adaptation borrowed from prior work (Zhang et al. 2024). The contribution is primarily combining existing ideas for VLODs rather than algorithmic innovation

Modest improvements in critical scenarios: driving scenes show only +1.0 mAP average gain despite being important applications; extreme corruptions (severity 5) yield minimal improvements, limiting practical utility
Fundamental limitation acknowledged but unaddressed: method underperforms on scenes with small, low-overlap objects (e.g., Cityscapes driving), a critical application domain
Significant hyperparameter sensitivity with dataset-dependent optimal values (θ varies 0.5-0.7 across datasets; λ requires 0.3 vs 0.1 for different architectures), raising generalization concerns
Incomplete ablation analysis: no clear breakdown of IWE vs IPS contributions to overall improvements; missing ablations showing each component's individual effect

Prompt generation compromise: dataset-specific prompts substantially outperform generic GPT prompts (Figure 4, +1.7 vs +1.2), but main results use generic prompts for 'realistic TTA,' undermining IPS potential and weakening results
Computational overhead not adequately justified: 4.4× slower than zero-shot (20 FPS vs 89 FPS) with claimed 'favorable robustness-cost trade-off' not substantiated for real-time applications
Fine-tuning unexpectedly degrades performance on style shifts (Section A.10) with insufficient analysis of underlying cause, suggesting brittleness
Batch size dependency problematic: performance improves then degrades with batch size (Figure 10a), yet method uses batch size 1 without thorough justification
Weak baseline comparisons: adapted baselines may not be optimally tuned; no comparison with other recent TTA-OD methods; claims about heavy augmentations in baselines not systematically verified

strengths: First TTA framework for vision-language object detectors, addressing a practically important and previously unexplored problem

Well-motivated technical components: IWE addresses genuine confirmation bias in entropy minimization for detection, and IPS provides principled alternative to prompt averaging with clear empirical benefits

Comprehensive experimental validation: 7 datasets, 96 test scenarios, 2 architectures, consistent improvements across diverse distribution shifts (stylized +3.3 mAP, driving +1.0 mAP, low-light +1.9 mAP, corruptions +3.9 mAP)

Thorough ablation studies including hyperparameter sensitivity, adapter placement, prompt strategies, batch size, augmentations, backbones, and fine-tuning effects, providing valuable insights into method behavior
Excellent presentation with effective motivating figures (Figures 1-2) that clearly demonstrate problems with standard approaches and benefits of proposed solutions
Practical efficiency: lightweight adapters (1.61M parameters), single adaptation step, reasonable computational trade-off (20 FPS vs 89 FPS baseline)
Extensive appendix with additional analyses (COCO-C, qualitative entropy comparison) and honest discussion of limitations
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty in individual components: IWE combines existing ideas (IoU weighting + entropy minimization) in straightforward way; IPS is essentially ranking and top-ρ selection; residual parameter borrowed from prior work. Overall contribution is engineering-focused rather than conceptually novel

Significant acknowledged limitations: method underperforms on small-object-heavy datasets (modest gains ≤1.6 mAP on Cityscapes/BDD100K), exactly where autonomous driving—a critical application—struggles. Conclusion admits IWE 'can underperform in scenes dominated by tiny, low-overlap objects'

Hyperparameter sensitivity with dataset dependence: multiple hyperparameters (θ, γ, λ, ρ, M) show non-trivial variation across datasets (e.g., θ: 0.5-0.7 depending on object size); despite claims of stability, practical deployment may require per-dataset tuning

Prompt pool dependency: method requires T=16 diverse prompts; performance sensitive to prompt quality (GPT-generated >> CLIP-style); dataset-specific prompts help significantly but violate true TTA assumptions; limits applicability where prompt engineering isn't straightforward

Baseline comparison concerns: several baselines (TPT, VPT, DPE) adapted from classification methods may not be optimally designed for detection; missing direct comparison with other OD TTA approaches adapted in same framework; Adapter baseline (closest method) could merit greater emphasis

Limited theoretical justification: no formal analysis of why cluster-size weighting with exponent γ is optimal or how this connects to distribution shift theory; incomplete explanation of architecture-specific design choices (YW needs vision adaptation, GD needs text adaptation)

Architecture-specific design requiring re-tuning: different adapter placement for YOLO-World vs Grounding DINO suggests limited generalizability; unclear how method would perform on other VLOD architectures without modification

Single adaptation step limits potential: Figure 10(b) suggests multi-step adaptation could improve results; no exploration of cumulative or batch-based strategies despite known benefits in TTA literature

Design choices lack sufficient justification: top-M=600 threshold for IoU graph appears arbitrary; no ablation on M beyond Figure 8; limited discussion of when standard entropy would be preferable; insufficient failure case analysis beyond small objects

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification with clear illustration of limitations in standard TTA approaches for VLODs through Figures 1-2
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 distinct domain shifts and 15 corruption types using two representative VLODs (YOLO-World and Grounding DINO)
Consistent improvements with all shifts evaluated: +3.3 mAP on YOLO-World and +2.4 mAP on Grounding DINO, across multiple corruption scenarios
Thorough ablation studies (Tables 3-4, 6-7) and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (Figure 6) clearly demonstrate individual component contributions
Honest treatment of limitations including failure case analysis (Cityscapes challenges), latency tradeoffs, and performance on specialized domains (Aquarium)
Clear mathematical formulations with detailed supplementary material, implementation details, and practical considerations for reproducibility
Comparison with relevant baselines including prior TTA methods (TPT, VPT, DPE, Adapter) and TTAOD-F, the only prior TTA method for VLODs
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: IWE is entropy minimization with IoU-based graph weighting (incremental spatial consistency enhancement), and IPS is straightforward prompt selection via compatibility scoring; both are relatively straightforward extensions of existing techniques
Latency claims are problematic: Table 7 shows 551.6 ms/img on YW versus TPT (211.6 ms/img) and VPT (470.9 ms/img), contradicting 'low overhead' claims; only faster than Adapter, not most baselines

Significant hyperparameter tuning burden undermines test-time adaptation claims: requires tuning θ, γ, λ, ρ, M, batch size, and dataset-specific learning rates; Figure 6 shows sharp performance drops outside optimal ranges
Limited generalization: evaluation restricted to two transformer-based VLODs; no demonstration on CNN-based VLODs despite claims of generality
Domain-specific failures inadequately addressed: Cityscapes shows poor performance due to small objects and label overlap, with identified problems but no solutions proposed
Lack of theoretical justification: no formal analysis of why IWE reduces confirmation bias or theoretical connection between spatial coherence and performance improvement; no convergence guarantees

Prompt generation strategy limitations: relies on ChatGPT-generated prompts (potential biases), shows dataset-specific prompts provide larger gains (unrealistic for test-time), limited exploration of prompt pool effects on IPS

Fine-tuning dependency obscures results: Tables 9-10 show substantial performance drops without pre-adaptation fine-tuning, suggesting approach requires careful setup; comparison with warm-start variant (VLOD-TTA*) uses different initialization

strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear practical relevance: VLODs suffer from distribution shift despite strong zero-shot performance, and existing TTA methods incur prohibitive overhead
Comprehensive experimental validation across 8+ datasets with diverse domain shifts (style, driving, illumination, corruptions) and detailed ablation studies quantifying component contributions
Practical efficiency with modest trainable parameters (1.61M) and low latency compared to prior TTA methods, suitable for deployment-constrained scenarios
Consistent improvements across most benchmarks indicating robustness to different types of distribution shift
Honest acknowledgment of limitations (Section 6.3) regarding small objects and crowded scenes rather than overclaiming generality
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: Both IWE (entropy minimization with IoU-weighted spatial consistency) and IPS (image-conditioned prompt selection) are straightforward combinations of existing techniques without significant algorithmic innovation

Modest and inconsistent empirical gains that often fail to justify added complexity: improvements over strong Adapter baseline are frequently <1 mAP; driving scenes show only +1.0 mAP despite being practically important

Critical practical limitation contradicts TTA assumptions: paper admits 'batch norm required dataset-specific learning-rate tuning' (Table 4), requiring labeled validation data that true TTA settings don't provide
Unresolved fundamental limitations acknowledged but not addressed: small objects, weak proposal overlap, and crowded scenes severely constrain effectiveness with no proposed solutions

Incomplete comparison with prior VLOD TTA method (TTAOD-F): VLOD-TTA* variant uses warm-start initialization making it unclear whether improvements stem from proposed components or simply better initialization

High hyperparameter sensitivity requiring tuning (Figure 6): IoU threshold θ, cluster exponent γ, number of proposals M, fusion coefficient λ, and selection fraction ρ all significantly affect performance, reducing robustness claims
Limited scope restricted to vision-language detectors only; doesn't generalize to closed-set detectors, reducing potential impact and applicability

Theoretical justification lacking: intuitive motivation (e.g., IoU overlap indicating proposal reliability) not rigorously established; design choices like IoU weighting scheme appear somewhat arbitrary
Evidence that simpler approaches may suffice: Adapter baseline remains surprisingly competitive, raising questions about whether full TTA framework is necessary versus simple backbone adaptation

strengths: Well-motivated technical contribution with clear problem identification (Figures 1-2) and principled solutions through spatial coherence weighting (IWE) and image-conditioned prompt selection (IPS)

Exceptionally comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 datasets covering multiple distribution shift types (stylized domains, autonomous driving, corruptions) with 15 corruption types at varying severity levels
Thorough ablation studies, hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, and comparative evaluation against multiple baselines (TPT, VPT, DPE, Adapter, TTAOD-F) demonstrating contribution of each component
Honest discussion of limitations and failure cases (small objects, sparse proposals, label ambiguity) with detailed analysis of method behavior and adapter placement effectiveness
Practical considerations addressed including computational cost analysis (Table 5), latency-accuracy trade-offs, and efficiency-performance comparison across methods
Clear presentation with effective motivation figures, intuitive method overview (Figure 3), and comprehensive visualization of results across multiple experimental settings
weaknesses: Incremental novelty relative to prior work TTAOD-F, with improvements primarily in avoiding teacher decoder overhead and replacing entropy minimization with IWE and prompt averaging with IPS—core algorithmic concepts are not substantially novel

Significant performance variability across distribution shifts: strong gains on stylized domains (+3-4 mAP) but weak improvements on driving scenarios (+1.0-1.8 mAP), suggesting limited generalization and utility in real-world deployment scenarios
Substantial computational overhead remains with 851.6 ms/img latency (vs. 701.9 for TTAOD-F) and ~1.61M parameters, questioning practical deployability despite efficiency claims
Method effectiveness is distribution-dependent without principled characterization of when TTA should be applied versus relying on zero-shot; no predictive framework for applicability
Hyperparameter sensitivity across multiple parameters (θ, γ, M, λ, ρ) with fixed values across all datasets potentially suboptimal, but limited guidance on per-dataset tuning
Limited evaluation scope restricted to YOLO-World and Grounding DINO; generalization to other VLOD architectures (OWLv2, etc.) remains unclear
Individual component contributions are relatively straightforward—IoU-based weighting for entropy and image-conditioned prompt selection are incremental extensions of existing TTA techniques
Batch size dependency (Figure 7a) limits practical single-image deployment, and paper does not adequately address this practical constraint
